title: PA/Secretary
description:
Personal Assistant

We are seeking a highly organised, proactive and professional Personal Assistant to provide comprehensive administrative and secretarial support to Executive Directors

This is a fast-paced and varied role where you will be responsible for managing complex diaries, coordinating meetings, handling confidential correspondence and ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of the Executive Directors' portfolios. The successful candidate will act as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders and play a vital role in supporting senior leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Executive Support
- Manage complex and constantly changing diaries.
- Coordinate meetings, appointments and travel arrangements.
- Monitor and manage Executive Directors' email inboxes.
- Handle incoming and outgoing correspondence.
- Prioritise enquiries and respond appropriately on behalf of Executive Directors.
- Prepare reports, presentations and professional documentation.

Meeting & Committee Support
- Organise and attend Board and Committee meetings.
- Produce accurate minutes and action logs.
- Prepare agendas and circulate papers to agreed deadlines.
- Track actions and ensure timely follow-up.
- Maintain meeting records and governance documentation.

Stakeholder Management
- Build effective relationships with colleagues, senior leaders, external partners and regulatory bodies.
- Act as a professional ambassador for the organisation.
- Manage sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
- Deal professionally with complex enquiries and challenging situations.

Administrative & Office Management
- Maintain electronic and paper filing systems.
- Ensure accurate record keeping and document management.
- Support projects and ad hoc work as required.
- Contribute to the continuous improvement of office processes and systems.
- Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence.

What We're Looking For
Essential
- Significant recent experience providing PA support at Director or Senior Manager level.
- Experience managing multiple priorities and competing deadlines.
- Experience taking minutes at senior-level meetings and committees.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Ability to handle sensitive information with confidentiality and professionalism.
- Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
- Ability to work proactively, independently and under pressure
- Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving abilities.
- Experience working within healthcare

Personal Qualities

We are looking for someone who:
- Is highly organised and dependable.
- Has exceptional interpersonal and communication skills.
- Remains calm and effective under pressure.
- Is confident working with senior stakeholders.
- Demonstrates initiative and excellent judgement.
- Can adapt quickly to changing priorities and business needs.
- Models the organisation's values of Kindness, Respect, Trust and Honesty

title: Administrator (Migration Support)
description:
Job Title: Administrator (Migration Support)

Location: Worksop, Nottinghamshire (S80 1 DH)

Pay Rate: 15.00 - 18.00 per hour (dependant on experience)

Start Date: Monday 5th October 2026

Hours: 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 5:00pm

Hybrid Working: 60% remote, 40% office-based (3 days from home, 2 days in office)

Join a Business Transforming the Rental Experience:

Lloyds Living is on an exciting journey to become one of the UK's most trusted and respected residential landlords. As we continue to grow and evolve, we are seeking a highly organised and detail-focused Migration Support Coordinator to join our Special Operations team.

This is an excellent opportunity to play a key role in a major business transformation programme, supporting the migration of property portfolios into Lloyds Living's operating model. Working closely with Migration Compliance Managers and the Migration Lead, you will help ensure critical information, documentation and records are accurately managed, reviewed and validated throughout the migration process.

What You'll Be Doing:

Migration Administration & Document Management:
- Organising and maintaining migration files, folders and document repositories.
- Managing and categorising documentation received from managing agents and internal stakeholders.
- Ensuring records are accurately named, version-controlled and stored correctly.
- Supporting the preparation of migration work packs, trackers and handover documentation.
- Maintaining clear and auditable records of documentation received, reviewed and outstanding.

Information Gathering & Validation:
- Collecting information from managing agents, business stakeholders and internal systems.
- Reviewing documentation for accuracy, consistency and completeness.
- Identifying missing, incomplete or inconsistent information and escalating where required.
- Completing validation activities against established quality standards and checklists.
- Supporting reviews of tenancy, property, compliance, financial and operational records.

Migration Project Support:
- Assisting Migration Compliance Managers with due diligence activities.
- Supporting portfolio readiness assessments and migration planning.
- Maintaining trackers, action logs and issue registers.
- Monitoring outstanding information requests and proactively following up with stakeholders.
- Supporting governance meetings, migration milestones and operational handovers.

Quality Assurance & Compliance:
- Following established migration procedures, controls and governance requirements.
- Conducting quality checks on documentation and migration records.
- Highlighting potential compliance, data quality or documentation concerns.
- Supporting audit readiness and accurate record keeping throughout migration projects.
- Assisting with management information and progress reporting.

Stakeholder Coordination:
- Supporting communication between internal teams and external managing agents.
- Responding professionally to information requests.
- Providing updates on progress, risks and outstanding actions.
- Supporting the wider Special Operations team in delivering successful migration outcomes.

What We're Looking For:

Essential Skills & Experience:
- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
- Previous experience in an administration, operations, compliance, project support or property-related role.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
- Confidence working with large volumes of documentation and data.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Outlook, Teams and the wider Microsoft Office suite.
- Ability to quickly learn new processes and follow structured procedures.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and investigating discrepancies.

About Lloyds Banking Group:

Lloyds Banking Group is committed to building a diverse, inclusive and supportive workplace where everyone can thrive. We celebrate individuality and are dedicated to creating an environment where colleagues can be themselves and perform at their best.

As a Disability Confident Leader, Lloyds Banking Group offers workplace adjustments wherever reasonable and supports applicants throughout the recruitment process. If you require any adjustments, we'll be happy to discuss how we can support you.

title: Sales Support Executive
description:
Sales Support Executive

Are you an organised and commercially aware sales support professional with experience preparing quotations, coordinating customer requests and supporting account activity? Ocular has a great opportunity for someone who enjoys providing proactive customer support, working closely with technical teams and helping deliver a faster, more efficient sales process. This role is officially known as a Sales and Quotations Executive.

If you've also worked in the following roles, we'd also like to hear from you: Internal Sales Coordinator, Sales Coordinator, Sales Administrator, Sales Support Coordinator, Quotations Coordinator, Quotations Administrator, Account Coordinator, Customer Account Coordinator, Sales Office Administrator, Internal Account Coordinator.

SALARY: £30,000 to £35,000 per annum + Benefits

LOCATION: Nottingham, Nottinghamshire, East Midlands - currently based in Beeston, with relocation to a new site near M1 Junction 27 planned for the end of 2026

JOB TYPE: Full-Time, Permanent

JOB OVERVIEW

This is an excellent opportunity for a Sales Support Executive to play a key role in managing customer quotation requests, coordinating technical information and supporting a smooth, efficient sales process.

As the Sales Support Executive, you will act as a central point of contact for customer quotation enquiries, prepare and track quotes, liaise with technical colleagues and ensure all activity is accurately recorded in the CRM system.

The Sales Support Executive will also support a defined base of smaller customer accounts through a structured contact cycle, following up outstanding quotations, maintaining customer records and identifying opportunities for additional Ocular solutions and services where appropriate.

ABOUT US

Ocular is an independent security systems integrator with over four decades of experience delivering security solutions across high-security, public space, transport, and infrastructure projects throughout the UK and Ireland.

The company is committed to building long-lasting customer relationships by delivering exceptional service at every stage. Through strong partnerships with leading technology providers, Ocular remains at the forefront of innovation, delivering reliable, tailored security solutions to meet each customer's unique requir

As part of Synectics Plc, our company values underpin everything we do, and we consistently recognise individuals within our business who demonstrate these behaviours.

APPLY TODAY

Ready to make your next career move? Apply Now for our Recruitment Team to review.

DUTIES

Your duties as the Sales Support Executive include:
- Manage Customer Quotations: Act as the primary point of contact for customer quotation requests, ensuring a fast, efficient and professional response
- Prepare and Track Quotes: Prepare, issue and follow up quotations, coordinating with the Technical Design team on technical content and specifications
- Qualify Incoming Requests: Review, qualify and prioritise customer requests before passing them to Design, helping reduce internal delays and rework
- Own the Quotation Process: Manage quotation activity for smaller accounts from initial request through to follow-up and close
- Maintain Commercial Governance: Ensure quotations are qualified, prioritised and commercially reviewed before issue
- Update CRM Records: Maintain a clear audit trail of quotation activity, account records, customer contact details and pipeline information within CRM
- Support Customer Accounts: Look after a defined base of smaller customer accounts through a structured, tiered call cycle
- Conduct Account Reviews: Carry out regular proactive account reviews and scheduled customer calls, rather than only responding when requirements arise
- Identify Customer Needs: Spot additional customer requirements and opportunities for wider Ocular solutions and services where appropriate
- Support Retention Activity: Support renewal, retention and ongoing relationship management activity across the managed account base
- Report Sales Activity: Provide clear visibility of quotation pipeline, conversion activity and account contact progress, reporting against KPIs as required
- Escalate Strategic Opportunities: Flag larger, strategic or multi-site opportunities for handover to senior or strategic account management colleagues

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS
- Previous experience in a sales support, internal sales or quotations role
- Experience gained within a technical, project-based or B2 B environment would be ideal
- Confident managing customer calls, written communication and quotation follow-up activity
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage a high volume of quotations and customer accounts
- Commercial awareness with the ability to qualify and prioritise opportunities
- Comfortable coordinating with technical teams to help translate customer requirements into accurate quotations
- Accurate CRM and system discipline, with strong attention to detail
- Collaborative approach, working closely with Technical Design and senior Sales colleagues

Successful applicants must be able to provide verification of their eligibility to live and work in the UK before starting employment

Our Commitment to Equality and Diversity

Synectics plc and its subsidiaries are committed to promoting equal opportunities in employment and in our employment policies for recruitment, selection, training, development, and promotion. Such policies are in place to ensure that both job applicants and employees of Synectics receive equal treatment regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

NO AGENCIES PLEASE

HOW TO APPLY

To be considered for this job vacancy, please submit your CV to our Recruitment Team who will review your details.

title: Supplier Support Coordinator
description:
Do you enjoy delivering excellent customer service and building strong relationships with customers and suppliers? Are you someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, resolving queries, coordinating with multiple stakeholders and ensuring a seamless service experience? If so, we'd love to hear from you.

Here at GXO, we're looking for a Supplier Support Coordinator to join our team in Nottingham, supporting our transport solution EyeQ across our network. In this role, you'll act as a key point of contact for customers, suppliers, drivers and internal teams, helping to deliver an exceptional customer experience while ensuring operational processes run smoothly.

This is a full-time, permanent position working Monday to Friday (37.5 hours per week) with flexibility between 07:30 and 17:00 to support business needs.

Pay, benefits and more:

We're looking to offer a salary of up to £26,100 per annum and 25 days annual leave (plus bank holidays). Your benefits package includes a company sponsored pension scheme, life assurance and access to our benefits platform, including retail discounts!

What you'll do on a typical day:
- Act as a key point of contact for customers, suppliers and operational teams, delivering a responsive and professional service
- Build and maintain strong relationships with external suppliers, supporting service performance and continuous improvement
- Manage customer and supplier enquiries, investigating and resolving issues while providing timely updates to stakeholders
- Communicate with drivers, customer sites and internal departments regarding delivery schedules, delays and service-related queries
- Monitor service performance and maintain accurate records, system updates and transport administration to support operational excellence

What you need to succeed at GXO:
- Previous experience in a customer service, logistics, transport or operational support environment
- Excellent communication skills with the ability to build strong relationships with customers, suppliers and colleagues
- A proactive and customer-focused approach with strong problem-solving skills
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work accurately under pressure
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications, with experience of transport systems being advantageous

We engineer faster, smarter, leaner supply chains.

GXO is a leading provider of cutting-edge supply chain solutions to the most successful companies in the world. We help our customers manage their goods most efficiently using our technology and services. Our greatest strength is our global team - energetic, innovative people of all experience levels and talents who make GXO a great place to work. GXO is an equal opportunity employer. title: Apprentice Talent Acquisition Coordinator
description:
Full-Time - Monday-Friday - Hybrid - L3 apprenticeship in Recruitment (18 months)

Salary: £25,311 per annum

Looking to start your career in Recruitment and Talent Acquisition?

Are you organised, confident communicating with people, and eager to learn? Do you enjoy building relationships and want to develop a career in recruitment while gaining a nationally recognised qualification?

If so, why not start your recruitment journey with Staffline?

Apprentice Talent Acquisition Coordinator

This is a hybrid role, splitting your time between working from home and our Nottingham office.

As an Apprentice Talent Acquisition Coordinator, you'll join our Talent Acquisition team while completing a Level 3 Recruitment Apprenticeship over 18 months. You'll gain hands-on experience supporting recruitment activities across a variety of roles while developing the skills and knowledge needed for a successful career in Talent Acquisition.

Working closely with the Talent Acquisition team, hiring managers and candidates, you'll help deliver a positive and efficient recruitment experience from attraction through to onboarding.

What you'll do as an Apprentice Talent Acquisition Coordinator

This is a fantastic opportunity to learn from experienced recruitment professionals and develop your career with the UK's largest recruiter.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Supporting the Talent Acquisition team with recruitment activity across a range of vacancies.
- Advertising vacancies across job boards, social media channels and other attraction platforms.
- Sourcing potential candidates and building talent pipelines.
- Screening applications and carrying out initial candidate conversations.
- Coordinating interviews and maintaining communication with candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Supporting hiring managers with recruitment administration and scheduling.
- Maintaining accurate candidate records within recruitment systems.
- Providing regular updates to candidates and stakeholders to ensure a positive recruitment experience.
- Supporting recruitment projects, employer branding initiatives and talent attraction campaigns.
- Completing your Level 3 Recruitment Resourcer Apprenticeship and applying your learning within the workplace.

What you'll need to succeed

We're looking for someone with enthusiasm, curiosity and a genuine interest in developing a career in recruitment.

You'll ideally have:
- A strong interest in recruitment, Talent Acquisition or Human Resources.
- Excellent communication skills and confidence speaking with a range of people.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks.
- Good attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records.
- A positive attitude and willingness to learn.
- The ability to build relationships and work collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
- The ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
- GCSEs (or equivalent) in English and Maths would be advantageous.

What you'll gain
- A Level 3 Recruitment Apprenticeship qualification.
- Hands-on experience within an in-house Talent Acquisition team.
- Ongoing support and mentoring from experienced recruitment professionals.
- Opportunities to develop your recruitment, sourcing and stakeholder management skills.
- A strong foundation for a long-term career in Talent Acquisition and HR.

Why join us?

This role offers the opportunity to develop your recruitment career within a supportive Talent Acquisition team, working across a variety of business areas while gaining valuable in-house recruitment experience.

Like the sound of this? Apply now, or get in touch with the Talent Acquisition team for further information.

title: Practice Administrator
description: We are delighted to offer an exciting opportunity to join Belvoir Health Group as a Practice Administrator. We are looking for enthusiastic, organised and motivated administrators to join our team on a full-time or part-time basis. The successful candidates will provide essential administrative support across our practices, helping to ensure the smooth and efficient delivery of high-quality patient care. The role offers a varied range of administrative responsibilities, including processing incoming correspondence, maintaining accurate patient records, summarising medical records and accurately coding clinical information. We are looking for someone who is highly organised, self-motivated and able to work independently, with excellent attention to detail. Previous administrative experience is essential, and experience within a healthcare or primary care setting would be an advantage. In return, we offer a supportive working environment, opportunities to develop your skills and experience, and access to the NHS Pension Scheme. The Practice Administrator will provide administrative support across the practice, with responsibility for maintaining accurate and up-to-date patient records. Key responsibilities will include: Processing incoming correspondence and clinical documentation in a timely and accurate manner. Scanning, attaching and accurately coding correspondence to the correct patient record. Reviewing clinical documentation and ensuring relevant information is accurately recorded within the practice clinical system. Assigning appropriate diagnosis and procedure codes in accordance with practice procedures and coding guidance. Summarising new patient medical records to ensure key clinical information is accurately captured and readily available to clinicians. Maintaining accurate and up-to-date electronic medical records in accordance with practice standards. Identifying and appropriately processing information received from hospitals, community services and other healthcare providers. Ensuring all patient information is handled securely and confidentially in accordance with GDPR, NHS requirements and practice policies. Working collaboratively with colleagues across the practice and contributing to the effective running of the administrative team. Undertaking any other appropriate administrative duties required to support the smooth operation of the practice. Job Description - Practice Administrator Role in Practice - Maintain accurate records, file medical notes, input data, word processing and scanning documents into the computer system. Responsible to - Team Leader Summary - The post-holder will be responsible for providing effective and efficient administrative support to the Partners and other Professional staff. Responsibilities - Administration To have a thorough knowledge of all practice procedures including summarising, private work, deductions, immunisations, scanning and coding and other administrative tasks as required To work in accordance with written protocols Accurately retrieving filing of both electronic and paper notes and updating demographic information as necessary Filing post including scanning test results and clinical correspondence into in medical records Dealing with incoming post Computer Registration of new patients computer data entry and making amendments to medical records Process patients change of address and other demographic information inputting computer data and medical records, having knowledge of the practice area and data protection protocols Knowledge of Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel messages clearly and accurately Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately according to the Data Protection Act and other information governance guidelines and employees will receive regular training regarding this. In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Other Tasks Ability to work within a team Lock up the building where required Be familiar with and adhere to Practice policies and procedures ensuring that patient confidentiality is maintained at all times Possess the ability to self-motivate, organise and prioritise own workload To participate in further professional development training courses to be discussed in consultation with line manager To undertake other responsibilities, within the scope of the grade You are requested to be flexible and the Partners reserve the right to alter such fixed hours as may be considered necessary to ensure the Practice runs smoothly.
